uncited: SDF Domain Manipulation Operators are a family of functions that modify the input query point $\mathbf{p}$ before evaluating a base Signed Distance Function (SDF) primitive.

Unlike [CSG Operations on Implicit Functions](1329-csg-operations-on-implicit-functions.md) which combine multiple SDFs by modifying the output distance value, domain operators modify the input coordinate $\mathbf{p}$ [1730-sdf-domain-manipulation-operators.md].

All domain manipulation operators follow a common mechanism: they accept a query point $\mathbf{p}$ (and often additional parameters) and return a transformed point $\mathbf{p}'$ (or modify $\mathbf{p}$ in place) which is then passed to the base SDF evaluation.
The general form is $d_{result}(\mathbf{p}) = d_{base}(T(\mathbf{p}))$, where $T$ is the transformation function.
The concept of manipulating the domain of a function to generate geometry is foundational in procedural modeling and ray marching.
These operators allow for the creation of intricate patterns like grids, spirals, and twisted structures by simply transforming the input coordinates before the distance calculation.
The technique is widely used in real-time graphics, shader coding, and procedural generation due to its computational efficiency and lack of need for explicit mesh data.
